 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifier: Chelle on trial as Super Eagles fight for survival in Zanzibar
 Chelle (left) led the Super Eagles to their official training session at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar yesterday. 
 Christian Okpara 
 17 November 2026 
 4:00 AM WAT 
 2 min read 
 Get Guardian on Google 
 Super Eagles ’ Coach, Eric Chelle, enters one of the most important battles of his career as Super Eagles’ coach in Tanzania today knowing that defeat will bring his tenure as manager of the senior national team to question.
 When the Franco-Malian took over the Super Eagles and failed to rescue their fading hope of playing at the 2026 World Cup, many followers of the game did not blame him much because he inherited a team that was in a bad shape both mentally and in the race for the Mundial.
 Nigeria was then marooned in fifth place in a six-team race with only two points from three and needed to win all its remaining games to qualify for the World Cup. The Super Eagles fell short of that and even lost the opportunity presented by the African playoff to make the Mundial by losing via penalties to DR Congo in the final game.

 Since then, Nigerians have given the former Mali manager the benefit of the doubt, hoping that he would rebuild the team and bring them at par with other African leading teams like Morocco, Senegal, Egypt and Cote d’Ivoire.
 Advertisement 
 But a 3-0 loss to Guinea Bissau early in the race for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations ticket has cast shadows on his ability to lead the team to glory any time soon.
 Guinea Bissau won by 2-0 against Tanzania in this same Zanzibar and if the Eagles fail to beat the same Taifa Stars, they may fall further behind the Group L leaders in the race, which consequence is missing the 2027 AFCON to be co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
 That is a prospect that could be too difficult for Chelle’s employers, the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), to explain to Nigerians, especially if the country also fails to qualify for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
 Chelle also manages the U-23 Eagles, who trail DR Congo 0-2 from the first leg of their qualifying tie. The decisive second leg will hold in Ikenne, also today.
 Advertisement 
 The Super Eagles are much aware that a different challenge awaits them on Tanzanian soil, where the hosts will be eager to make a statement in front of their supporters. For Tanzania , today’s encounter presents an opportunity to respond in front of home fans after their defeat in Uyo.
 Although the Taifa Stars have already secured their place at the 2027 AFCON finals as co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda, they will be determined to demonstrate their competitiveness against one of Africa’s football heavyweights.
 An exciting encounter is expected in Zanzibar from 2.00 p.m. Nigeria time.
 Three points in Zanzibar, against a side that had never beaten them in any of their previous 14 encounters, would represent another important step towards securing Nigeria’s place at the 2027 AFCON in East Africa.
